Google for Startups offers a wide variety of programs and initiatives to help connect startups of every stage and vertical to the right people, products, and best practices they need to grow and scale.

About the Gemini Startup Forum

Google for Startups, in partnership with DeepMind and Google Cloud, presents the Gemini Startup Forum. A curated gathering for seed to Series A founders to connect in person with experts from Google AI and explore what is possible at the frontier of AI.

[Find out more](https://startup.google.com/programs/gemini-startup-forum/)

From Google to you

A comprehensive series of guided online trainings, designed to equip early-stage startups with the tools, products, and knowledge that growing companies need.

Sign up for an upcoming edition of Startup School to access a series of live streamed lessons for startup founders and their teams. From Google Ads and Analytics, to YouTube and Google Cloud—join us and help your startup grow.

## A global series of programs

Each accelerator features a cohort of 10-15 top startups that come together to tackle specific technical challenges that can help grow their businesses through a mix of remote and in-person, 1-to-1, group learning sessions, and sprint projects.

## Dedicated expert help

Founders outline the top technical challenges for their startup, and are then paired with relevant experts from both Google and the industry to solve those challenges and grow their business.

## Specialist deep dives

In addition to mentorship and technical project support, Google for Startups Accelerators include deep dives and workshops focused on product design, customer acquisition, and leadership development for founders.

## Early access to AI products

Eligible participants receive Early Access Program and Trusted Tester benefits for Google’s AI products.

## Cloud credits

Eligible participants can apply for Google Cloud credits to support their business’ growth. [Find out more](https://cloud.google.com/startup?e=48754805).

## Cloud TPUs

Participants are eligible to receive free Cloud TPU access to accelerate open source machine learning research. [Find out more](https://sites.research.google/trc/about/).

Tech giant Google has unveiled the 20 startups selected for the 2025 cohort of its “Google for Startups Accelerator: AI First” programme. Chosen from more than 1,600 applications, the selected startups will undergo a three-month “equity-free” programme designed to help them tackle early-stage challenges and scale their businesses.

Targeted at seed to Series A startups, the accelerator offers mentorship from Google experts, technical training through bootcamps, access to Google Cloud and its in-house developed large language model (LLM) Gemini AI. Besides, eligible startups are also given $350K (around INR 3 Cr) worth Google Cloud credits.

Google launched the startup accelerator in April 2024 and subsequently [unveiled its first cohort of 20 startups last August](https://inc42.com/buzz/meet-the-20-startups-selected-for-googles-ai-first-accelerator/) after sifting through over 1,030 applications. The last cohort featured startups Kroop AI, Segwise.ai, Hypergro, among others.

The 2025 batch reflects emerging AI trends in India, with 45% of startups focused on agentic AI, 30% working on multimodal AI applications, and the remaining 25% building foundational models and responsible AI solutions.

Without further delay, let’s meet the 20 Indian AI startups part of the Google for Startups Accelerator: AI First cohort for 2025.

## **Adya**

**Founded In:** 2023

**Headquarters:** Mumbai

Founded by Shayak Mazumder, Archana Shah and Angad Singh Ahluwalia, Adya is an agentic AI platform that enables businesses to build, orchestrate, and deploy AI agents across functions such as sales, marketing, customer service, HR, and data analysis.

Its platform allows apps to be built from simple verbal prompts, with tools to manage and deploy AI agents effectively. The startup [raised INR 10.2 Cr](https://inc42.com/buzz/adya-ai-bags-funding-to-help-enterprises-build-apps-on-ondc/) from India Angel Network and IvyCap Ventures last year.

## **Aignosis**

**Founded In:** 2024

**Headquarters:** Jaipur

Aignosis, founded by Divyansh Mangal and Raksheet Jain, is a healthcare AI startup developing webcam-based tools to detect early signs of developmental and neurodevelopmental disorders in children, helping parents identify issues at an early stage.

## **AiSteth**

**Founded In:** 2019

**Headquartered:** Bengaluru

Founded by Satish S Jeevannavar and Ashwin Chandrasekaran, AiSteth has built an AI-powered smart stethoscope for early detection of cardio-respiratory conditions, enabling doctors to detect lung and heart anomalies more accurately.

## **Apptile**

**Founded In:** 2021

**Headquartered:** Bellevue, USA

Apptile, launched by Rohit Modi and Vishal Sood, uses AI to rapidly design, build, and deploy native mobile apps. It claims its apps drive 3X higher conversion rates, 7X engagement, and 5X more product views for businesses.

## **Dview**

**Founded In:** 2021

**Headquartered:** Bengaluru

Founded by Kauts Shukla and Supratik Shankar, Dview is an AI-native data platform that unifies diverse datasets to generate concurrent insights for faster business decision-making. The startup, backed by InfoEdge Ventures and Capital 2B, has raised $1.3 Mn.

## **Knit**

**Founded In:** 2019

**Headquartered:** Bengaluru

Knit, founded by Gaurav Bhawnani, Yasharth Mishra and Kunal Mishra, develops unified APIs to help SaaS products like HRMS and CRM systems integrate seamlessly. It also supports agentic AI startups by enabling their AI systems to connect with other SaaS tools.

## **Mili AI**

**Founded In:** 2024

**Headquartered**: San Francisco, USA

Founded by Chirag Gandhi, Vennela Miryala and Siddharth Bulia, Mili AI builds AI agents for financial advisors. These agents handle scheduling, note-taking, and follow-ups to streamline client management.

Latino Founders Fund recipient Waterplan

Everyday in my role at Google Research, I get a front row seat of the incredible progress our researchers are making in AI — but many of the most exciting developments aren't happening in our labs. Some of the most cutting-edge and inspiring innovations are coming from entrepreneurs, who combine their fresh perspectives and diverse experiences with our Google AI tools in order to build businesses and solve real-world problems. That's why today, we're excited to announce that we're funding 20 incredible companies through the [Google for Startups Founders Funds](https://startup.google.com/programs/founders-funds/) which provides equity-free capital and hands-on support to Black and Latino-led startups using AI to innovate responsibly and drive meaningful change.

These companies are pushing the boundaries of what's achievable with AI, from developing innovative solutions to prevent wildfires ( [Improving Aviation](https://www.improvingaviation.com/)), to diverting millions of tons of fast fashion from landfills ( [Sortile](https://www.sortile.co/)), and to helping millions of helping millions of community college learners successfully transfer and acquire four-year degrees ( [EdVisorly](https://edvisorly.com/)). These are just a few examples of the groundbreaking innovations that are emerging from this group of exceptional founders.

Each startup will receive $150,000 in non-dilutive cash awards, $100,000 in Google Cloud credits, and hands-on mentorship from Google experts across AI, sales and more to help build and scale their companies and innovate responsibly with AI.

Eligible startups will be matched with the tier and benefits that best suit the stage they are in. ### Program tiers to help startups build quickly and thrive

Eligibility and benefits

#### Start tier

Designed for startups who have not yet received equity funding.

Apply now [Apply now](https://cloud.google.com/startup/apply?)

#### Scale tier

Designed for funded startups with verified equity funding up to and including series A.

Apply now [Apply now](https://cloud.google.com/startup/apply?)

#### Eligibility requirements

- Technology startup not yet funded by an institutional investor

- Founded within the last 5 years

- Not yet received Google Cloud credits (beyond the free trial)


- Received startup equity funding\* from pre-seed to series A (if series A, raised within the last 12 months) by an institutional investor or common Web3 funding sources

- Founded within the last 10 years

- Not yet received more than $5,000 in Google Cloud credits

**Year 2:** 20% up to an additional $100,000 USD in Google Cloud credits \[1\]

- Access to Google Cloud Startup Customer Engineers


#### Business support and networking

- Access to our global Google Cloud Startup Community


- Access to a Startup Success Manager, our global Google Cloud Startup Community, and co-marketing opportunities for select startups


#### Google-wide discounts and perks

## FAQs

keyboard\_arrow\_up

#### What is the value of an accelerator?

- **Develop:** Solve a key technical challenge for your startup with Google experts. Receive strategic support and feedback on product design, growth, and founder leadership. Use Google product credits as you scale.
- **Learn:** Improve your skills through remote and in-person events, one-on-one and group learning sessions, and technical sprints. Gain access to experts, technical mentorship, and training to help you succeed.
- **Network:** Meet with industry and Google experts to solve core business challenges. Excel with project partnerships, resources, and access to a network of peers.

keyboard\_arrow\_up

#### What are your Accelerator programs?

Accelerators operate within specific geographies, industries, or causes. For a full list, visit the [program page](https://developers.google.com/community/accelerators/programs).

keyboard\_arrow\_up

#### Who should apply to an accelerator?

Each accelerator program has specific requirements.

- For Google for Startups Accelerators, high potential Series A to growth startups should apply.
- For the Indie Games Accelerator, you must be a registered developer on Google Play and be the developer of the game you are submitting for review.
- The Google.org Impact Challenge Accelerator covers a different focus for each class. Follow [Google.org](https://www.google.org/opportunities/) for more information on upcoming classes.

keyboard\_arrow\_up

#### How do I apply to join an accelerator class?

Each accelerator program has its own application process and deadlines. [Search for a program](https://developers.google.com/community/accelerators/programs) that fits your location and look for details on the dedicated page.

keyboard\_arrow\_up

#### What are accelerators' values?

Google is committed to significantly improving the lives of as many people as possible. Accelerators work to support that in various ways:

**Crisis response and economic recovery**

Accelerators support startups that work on solutions related to crisis response or the post-crisis economic recovery of a specific region. Accelerator alumni have also contributed to economic growth by hiring over 60,000 employees worldwide.

**A sustainable future**

The following accelerator programs are committed to supporting developers, startups, and nonprofits focused on solving the world's most pressing challenges, including sustainability:

- **Google.org Impact Challenge on Climate**


Part of an ongoing partnership with Google.org, the program partners with nonprofits working to make the world a healthier and more sustainable place.
- **Google for Startups Accelerator: Climate Change**


This program partners with technology-enabled startups that use AI and machine learning and are focused on solving issues related to climate change.
- **Google for Startups Accelerator: Circular Economy**


This program is designed to bring the best of Google's programs, products, people, network and technology to those working towards a waste-free world.

## About

To bring the benefits of AI to the social sector, Google launched the Google.org Accelerator: Generative AI in 2024, helping 21 organizations build gen AI-powered solutions that collectively expect to reach more than 30 million beneficiaries over the next three years.

In a recent Google.org survey, nearly two-thirds of nonprofits using AI tools reported feeling more confident in serving their organization’s mission when they use AI apps and features, yet only one in five say that at least half their organization uses generative AI. To help even more organizations harness gen AI for social impact, we launched an open call in January 2025 to find the next cohort.
